method: Fresh Chromium contexts; French localStorage preference; Brotli-Q4 local serving; cache disabled, service workers blocked, 80 ms RTT / 20 Mbps down / 2 Mbps up / 3x CPU; API traffic blocked; readiness requires splash opacity 0/removed and translated login UI visible.
limitations: This uses an app-local i18next/React-i18next compatibility adapter over generated messages and a static literal-call codemod; it is an experiment, not a supported migration API.

Service workers are blocked and cache disabled. The native PWA precaches all locales; split candidate build precaches all 51 locale chunks, so this captures first-route cold network only, not install/offline behavior.

The app imposes a 1,000 ms minimum splash duration plus a 300 ms logo fade and 100 ms background fade. First content paint often reflects the static splash, so route readiness is the more relevant user-facing measure.
Native frontend build artifacts were captured before modifying the isolated app worktree; this comparison covers /login and its requested asset graph, not every account/notification route.
FCP/LCP are the static splash rather than the translated login view and are excluded from the >=10% qualification gate.
